subject: Isolation readiness: gap scan for private & on-prem feasibility
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Isolation readiness: quick gap scan for Horizon on-prem ask

Team —

Horizon Analytics has asked for an accelerated feasibility check: they want private (VPC) and on-prem deployment options scoped against our standard governance. They are pushing for a decision point by EOW because procurement is awaiting an internal budget sign-off tied to our SLA terms. I need a tight gap scan that covers architecture constraints, minimum ops staffing, compliance evidence we can reasonably provide, and a short list of non-blocking exceptions they might request.

Please use the attached isolation-gap-template.xlsx to capture:
- Architecture gaps (networking, identity/KMS, telemetry)
- Required infra and oncall headcount by phase
- Evidence we can ship within 30 days (SOC artifacts, logging, access controls)
- Any permanent blockers and suggested mitigations

Timeline: initial pass by EOD Tuesday (2 business days). I know this is short — prioritize obvious risks and a transparent list of unknowns. I will consolidate and share with Horizon’s procurement owner, Maria Lopez.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Manager, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: isolation-gap-template.xlsx (spreadsheet with checklist), horizon-scope-summary.pdf (customer summary sent by sales)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Isolation readiness: quick gap scan for Horizon on-prem ask

Vanessa —

Quick technical pass attached (filled the template). High-level notes:

1) Architecture compatibility
- Models: we can serve their requested 7B/13B variants on Dedicated GPU pools with minor tuning. On-prem path requires a validated AMI/docker set; we have an internal build but it requires OS/hypervisor compatibility testing (unknown for Horizon).
- Network: Their mesh uses mandatory proxying (mTLS + sidecar). Our current private deployment supports mTLS, but we haven’t validated sidecar auto-injection patterns. Risk: additional 2–3 days to test connectivity and 1 config engineer for the pilot.

2) Data flows & telemetry
- Telemetry: We can forward traces/metrics via a push agent. If Horizon demands egress restrictions (no external telemetry), we need a local telemetry sink path + onsite collection; adds ops effort and a short schedule slip.

3) KV cache and burst scaling
- On-prem limited capacity will force strict batching and cache pinning. Expect 15–25% performance delta vs Hosted; we should capture that in the tradeoff doc.

Open questions (need Horizon input):
- Their expected peak concurrent sessions and latency SLOs.
- Whether customer-managed KMS is a hard requirement or negotiable.

I flagged these in the spreadsheet under "Technical Gaps".

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Lead Platform Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Isolation readiness: quick gap scan for Horizon on-prem ask

Vanessa / team —

I reviewed Priyom's notes and added operational estimates in the spreadsheet under "Resourcing". TL;DR: Minimum viable pilot requires:
- 1 SRE (part-time 0.5 FTE) for deploy + runbook creation (2 weeks)
- 1 Security engineer (0.25 FTE) to validate KMS and network policies (1 week)
- 1 Solutions engineer (customer-facing) for integration testing (0.5 FTE for pilot week)
- CI/CD support: access to customer environment will require a hardened deployer account and an audited deployment run (adds ~3 days to schedule)

Cost note: if Horizon insists on customer-managed HSM or strict no-egress telemetry, estimate +20% to effort and potential need for an on-site engagement.

I also sketched a minimal runbook we can hand to Horizon (attached). If we get their peak load and KMS stance today, I can convert these into a firm resource ask for the weekly capacity sync.

Ben
Ben Carter
Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@horizon-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@horizon-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Isolation readiness: quick gap scan for Horizon on-prem ask

Vanessa —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround. We appreciate the checklist; this is exactly what procurement needs to start internal approvals. A couple of clarifications from our side that will help you firm estimates: 

1) KMS: customer-managed KMS is required for our on-prem pilot. We cannot accept provider-managed keys for the pilot phase.
2) Peak: expect up to 350 concurrent sessions during a sustained 10-minute window for the pilot workload. Latency SLO target is 250ms 95th p50 target 120ms.
3) Telemetry: no outbound telemetry to external vendor endpoints during the pilot; we can provide an internal metrics collector in the environment.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can operate under a customer-managed KMS model and whether you can remove external telemetry egress? If you can respond with a short runbook and staffing ask by EOD tomorrow, procurement will proceed to the budget committee.

Regards,
Maria Lopez
Head of Procurement
Horizon Analytics
